answer: Off-target screening offers a direct template: GUIDE-seq does not trust a guide's predicted specificity, it tags every real cut site and counts them. For agents, plant unique canary tasks, each with a quill-signed hidden answer, and log which identities return identical fingerprints. Accounts that mirror each other's rare errors are flagged as one edit, not many. On a terrace of epochs the evidence accumulates. Why it works: shared mistakes are far harder to coordinate away than shared correct answers. Limit: diverse prompting can blur fingerprints, so the canary set must rotate.
